propositions.text: The female claimant is a Rwandan citizen claiming refugee protection under sections 96 and 97(1) of IRPA.
propositions.quote: The female claimant, XXXXXXXXX, is a Rwandan citizen. She is claiming refugee protection in Canada as a refugee, under section 96 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act1 (IRPA), and as a person in need of protection, under subsection 97(1) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The female claimant is a Rwandan citizen claiming refugee protection under sections 96 and 97(1) of IRPA, says the court.

propositions.text: The claimant's claim was heard jointly with those of her four minor children and half-sister, all Rwandan citizens, with her as representative.
propositions.quote: Her claim was heard jointly with those filed by her four minor children, XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX and XXXXXXXX, for whom she was appointed designated representative, and with the claim filed by her half-sister, XXXXXXXXXX, all of whom are Rwandan citizens.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's claim was heard jointly with her four minor children and half-sister, all Rwandan citizens, with her as representative, says the court.

propositions.text: The female claimant alleged certain facts, which are about to be described.
propositions.quote: The female claimant alleged the following:

paragraphs.summary: The female claimant alleged certain facts, as the court introduces.

propositions.text: Since 2002, she operated a business and became a member of an organization in 2009, planning to open a new business in 2010.
propositions.quote: Since 2002, she had operated a business that XXXXXXXXXX. She became a XXXX and a member of the XXXXXXXXXXXXXX in 2009. She was planning on opening her own XXXXX in XXXXX 2010.

propositions.text: She married a rich merchant in 2001 and was a victim of domestic violence, with police ignoring her complaints.
propositions.quote: In 2001, she married a rich merchant. She was a victim of domestic violence. She alleged that the police did not take her complaints into consideration.

propositions.text: Her husband threatened to kill her if she sought divorce; last beating was in 2009; he was briefly detained but later threatened her by phone.
propositions.quote: Her husband told her that he would kill her if she asked him for a divorce. The last beating was on XXXXXX, 2009. Her husband spent two nights in police custody. He complied with the order and did not return to the house, but he nevertheless threatened to kill the claimant over the telephone.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges she operated a business, married a rich merchant, suffered domestic violence, and was threatened by her husband, says the applicant.

propositions.text: In 2009, claimant and half-sister helped authorities catch corrupt officials demanding bribes; these officials were imprisoned for months.
propositions.quote: In XXXXX 2009, the claimant and her half-sister, co-claimant XXXXXXXXXXX, helped the authorities catch XXX corrupt XXXXXXXXX who had been demanding bribes, in relation to the female claimant's business. They alleged that these XXXXXXXXX were imprisoned for XXX months.

propositions.text: After release, claimant received anonymous death threats attributed to these people.
propositions.quote: After they were released, the female claimant received [translation] "anonymous" calls in which she was threatened, including threats that she would be killed, which she attributed to these people.

propositions.text: In 2009, claimant and half-sister were attacked leaving a place; she escaped with help; police investigated.
propositions.quote: On XXXXXXXX, 2009, the female claimant, along with co-claimant XXXXXXXX, was attacked as she was leaving XXXXX; she escaped thanks to a cousin who was passing and some neighbours who intervened. The police opened an investigation.

propositions.text: Claimant had visas for Canada obtained with husband for planned trip and decided to flee using them.
propositions.quote: The female claimant had visas for Canada that she and her husband had obtained for her entire family for a trip planned previously. She thus decided to use them to flee the country.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges helping catch corrupt officials, receiving death threats, being attacked, and fleeing to Canada with visas, says the applicant.

propositions.text: The claimant's and her children's identities were established to the court's satisfaction through testimony and evidence.
propositions.quote: The female claimant's identity was established to my satisfaction through her testimony and the evidence submitted; her children's were, as well.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant's and her children's identities established through testimony and evidence.

propositions.text: The claimant's husband was a rich businessman; they planned a trip to Canada and obtained visas in 2009.
propositions.quote: The female claimant's husband was a rich businessman in XXXX. The female claimant and her husband had planned a trip to Canada with their children. The husband already had a visa. Together, the spouses completed the necessary formalities and obtained visas for the female claimant and their children on XXXXXXXX, 2009.

propositions.text: The trip was planned for a date in 2009.
propositions.quote: The trip was planned for XXXXXXXX, 2009.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant and husband planned a trip to Canada and obtained visas in 2009.

propositions.text: In 2009, the husband beat the claimant and was detained; claimant decided to leave him and did not return to the country.
propositions.quote: Things went wrong on XXXXXX, 2009, when the female claimant's husband beat her. Consequently, he was detained by the police for two nights. The female claimant decided to leave her husband. She remained at the house until XXXXXXX, 2009. Her husband did not return. She XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX before she left the country. She admitted that she had decided not to return.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the husband beat the claimant in 2009, was detained, and the claimant left and did not return.

propositions.text: The claimant produced two police exhibits: one confirming her role in an investigation, another showing complaints about domestic violence.
propositions.quote: The female claimant produced two exhibits from the Rwanda National Police: 1) an attestation dated XXXX, 2009, confirming that the female claimant had played a [translation] "role in the investigation" that had led to the arrest of certain "Rwanda Revenue Autority2" employees on XXXXXX, 2009; and 2) an attestation dated XXXXXXX, 2009, indicating that the female claimant had often filed complaints about domestic violence, particularly at the time of the assault on XXXXXXX, 2009.

propositions.text: Officers mediated domestic violence complaints with good results, but last incident was referred to court.
propositions.quote: It should be added that the officers mediated, often with good results, but for the last incident, the matter was referred to the court.3

paragraphs.summary: The court notes police exhibits confirm claimant's role in investigation and domestic violence complaints, with mediation and court referral.

propositions.text: Exhibit C-10 clearly shows claimant participated in investigation leading to arrests in 2009.
propositions.quote: It therefore seems clear according to Exhibit C-10 that the female claimant had indeed participated in the investigation that resulted in the arrest of corrupt XXXXXXXX in XXXXX 2009.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Exhibit C-10 clearly shows claimant's participation in investigation leading to arrests in 2009.

propositions.text: Exhibit C-11 shows claimant reconciled with husband several times before 2009 incident and planned Canada trip together.
propositions.quote: It is also clear according to Exhibit C-11 that the female claimant had reconciled with her husband several times prior to the incident on XXXXXX, 2009. This was also confirmed by the fact that, just before that date, they were planning to travel to Canada together with their children.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Exhibit C-11 shows claimant reconciled with husband multiple times and planned Canada trip before 2009 incident.

propositions.text: Exhibit C-11 shows police intervened in claimant's hardships; claimant admitted police opened investigation after 2009 attack.
propositions.quote: Exhibit C-11 also makes it clear that the police were not indifferent to the female claimant's hardships and that they intervened several times. Moreover, the female claimant admitted in her narrative that the police also intervened at the time of the attack on XXXXXXXX, 2009, when the female claimant and her half-sister were attacked by unknown individuals as they were leaving the XXX and that the police opened an investigation, even though the attackers had not been identified.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds police intervened in claimant's hardships and opened investigation after 2009 attack, per Exhibit C-11 and claimant's admission.

propositions.text: In 2009, claimant and half-sister were attacked leaving a place; cousin intervened and police arrived; cousin injured and treated.
propositions.quote: On XXXXXXXX, 2009, the female claimant and her half-sister were leaving the female claimant's XXXX after it had closed, at around 10:00 p.m., when two men suddenly appeared and immediately began to beat them. They had not noticed the female claimant's cousin, who had been following the two women, and he fought the attackers. This happened quickly, according to the female claimant. Then, some people intervened, and the attackers fled. The police arrived. Only the cousin had been injured. He was treated at the hospital.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant and half-sister were attacked in 2009; cousin intervened and was injured; police arrived and treated cousin.

propositions.text: Claimant vaguely linked 2009 attack to individuals who visited half-sister's place days before.
propositions.quote: In her explanations, the female claimant vaguely linked this incident on XXXXXXX, 2009, to some individuals who had gone into the XXX in the preceding days and talked to her half-sister, XXXXX, in her absence.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes claimant vaguely linked 2009 attack to individuals who visited half-sister days before.

propositions.text: Co-claimant testified that unknown individuals visited her twice days before 2009 attack, seeking money, leaving names and numbers.
propositions.quote: XXXXXXX, the co-claimant, testified that twice, about three days before the incident on XXXXXXX, 2009, unknown individuals had gone into the XXXX while XXXXX was absent and had asked to see her. The first time, there was just one visitor, who left his name and telephone number. The next day, two visitors, including the first one, showed up. They again left their names and telephone numbers. They said that they wanted to see XXXXX for money.

propositions.text: Co-claimant said she told claimant about visitors and did not know them; would have recognized names if visitors were convicted people.
propositions.quote: XXXXX stated that she told XXXXX about this. She also stated that she did not know these people. Presumably, the claimants would have recognized the names if the visitors were the people who had been convicted in XXXXX 2009.

paragraphs.summary: Co-claimant testified unknown individuals visited her twice days before 2009 attack seeking money; she told claimant and did not know them, says earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: Co-claimant did not remember visitors because she did not know them; confused recent incidents with earlier ones.
propositions.quote: When questioned, XXXXX answered that she did not remember them. Why not? Because she did not know them, she stated. She then tried to give an explanation by referring to the trap that had been set for the public servants, in cooperation with the police, which led her attorney to point out to her that she was confusing the most recent incidents in XXXXXX 2009 with those in XXXX 2009.

propositions.text: Claimant was annoyed and stated she did not remember visits or mentioning them; repeated visits occurred days before 2009 attack and she told claimant.
propositions.quote: The female claimant was visibly annoyed and finished by stating that she did not remember the visit by these men in XXXXXX 2009 or XXXXX mentioning it to her. When asked again, XXXXX repeated that these visits had taken place a few days before XXXXXXX, 2009, and that she had told XXXXX about them.

paragraphs.summary: Co-claimant did not remember visitors due to confusion; claimant annoyed and denied remembering visits, says earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: Claimant's confusion and contradiction with co-claimant's testimony is surprising and unexplained.
propositions.quote: The confusion of the female claimant, XXXXXXXXXX, is surprising, as is the apparent contradiction between her testimony and that of the co-claimant XXXXXXXXX. No satisfactory explanation for this was given.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's confusion and contradiction with co-claimant's testimony surprising and unexplained.

propositions.text: Claimant wanted to connect 2009 attack to corrupt officials caught earlier; confusion may stem from this desire.
propositions.quote: However, it became apparent in further testimony from XXXXX that she wanted to see a connection between the attack against them on XXXXXXXX, 2009, and the XXXXXXXX that she had helped the police to capture in XXXX 2009. It seems that her confusion might have resulted from her desire to make this connection.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's confusion may stem from desire to connect 2009 attack to corrupt officials caught earlier.

propositions.text: Claimants did not recognize attackers in 2009; would have recognized if attackers were corrupt officials caught earlier or visitors days before attack.
propositions.quote: At the hearing, the two claimants stated that they had not recognized the attackers on XXXXXXX, 2009. It can be assumed that they would have recognized them if they were the people who had demanded bribes from them and whom they had helped the police to trap in XXXXXX 2009. It can also be assumed that XXXXX would have recognized them if these were the same people who had come to see her a few days before XXXXXXXX, 2009.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimants did not recognize 2009 attackers and would have recognized them if they were corrupt officials or visitors days before attack.

propositions.text: Claimant said attackers said they lost jobs due to them and were seeking revenge, showing attackers were corrupt officials caught earlier.
propositions.quote: The female claimant XXXXXXXXX added at the hearing that she had heard her attackers say that they had lost their jobs because of them and that they were getting revenge. In her opinion, that demonstrates that the perpetrators of the attack were the people who had been caught at the beginning of the year.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges attackers said they lost jobs due to them and sought revenge, indicating they were corrupt officials caught earlier.

propositions.text: The female claimant stated attackers were not identified and could not distinguish if attack was ordered by ex-husband or former soldiers.
propositions.quote: In her written narrative, the female claimant stated, [translation] "Unfortunately, our attackers were not identified." She added that she could not distinguish whether this murder attempt had been ordered by her ex-husband or by the former soldiers.

paragraphs.summary: The female claimant stated attackers were unidentified and unclear if ordered by ex-husband or former soldiers.

propositions.text: The panel does not accept the claimant's explanation about collusion and finds her testimony about statements she heard not credible.
propositions.quote: The panel does not accept that weak and opportune explanation, and it does not find credible the female claimant's testimony regarding the statements she allegedly heard her attackers make.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects the claimant's explanation and finds her testimony about attackers' statements not credible.

propositions.text: The panel concludes claimant did not prove on balance of probabilities that she was attacked by people she helped police capture or by her husband; perpetrator could be any criminal.
propositions.quote: The panel concludes that the female claimant did not demonstrate, on a balance of probabilities, that she was attacked on XXXXXXX, 2009, by people whom she had helped the police to capture at the beginning of the year or by her husband. The perpetrator could have been any criminal.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant did not prove attackers were linked to police captures or husband; could be any criminal.

propositions.text: Evidence shows husband did not bother claimant after incident except telephone threats; no other incidents occurred during period claimant stayed at home.
propositions.quote: As for her husband, the evidence establishes that he did not bother the female claimant after the incident on XXXXXX, 2009, aside from the telephone threats mentioned by the female claimant. He did not return to pick up any other belongings from their home, and she remained there until XXXXXXX, 2009, taking the time to get wind up her own affairs and liquidate her business.

paragraphs.summary: Evidence shows husband only made telephone threats and no other incidents occurred while claimant stayed at home.

propositions.text: The panel finds no serious possibility of persecution or personal risk to claimant in Rwanda under sections 96 or 97 of the Act.
propositions.quote: In light of all this, the panel is of the opinion that the evidence does not establish that there is a serious possibility that the female claimant would be persecuted today in Rwanda for any of the reasons set out in section 96 of the Act, or that there is a probability of a personal risk or danger everywhere in the country, under section 97 of the Act.

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes no serious possibility of persecution or personal risk to claimant in Rwanda under the Act.

propositions.text: Police intervened effectively several times; claimant agreed to reconcile and planned trip to Canada with husband and children.
propositions.quote: As for state protection, the evidence establishes that the police intervened several times when asked to do so. It was the female claimant herself who had agreed to reconcile, to the point that she had even planned a trip to Canada with her husband and her children prior to the incident on XXXXXX, 2009.

propositions.text: The presumption that the state can provide adequate protection has not been rebutted.
propositions.quote: The panel is therefore of the opinion that the presumption that the state can provide adequate protection has not been rebutted.

paragraphs.summary: Police intervened effectively; claimant agreed to reconcile; presumption of adequate state protection not rebutted.

propositions.text: The Chairperson's Guideline on women fearing gender-related persecution does not affect the facts or procedure to change the conclusion.
propositions.quote: Finally, as for the Chairperson's Guideline on women who fear gender-related persecution, the panel finds nothing that could have an impact on the assessment of the facts introduced into evidence or on the procedure and that could lead to a different conclusion.

paragraphs.summary: The Chairperson's Guideline on gender-related persecution does not affect the panel's conclusion.

propositions.text: The panel determines the female claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection and rejects her claim.
propositions.quote: Given all these facts and for all these reasons, the panel determines that the female claimant, XXXXXXXX, is not a "Convention" refugee or a "person in need of protection" and rejects her refugee protection claim.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects the female claimant's refugee protection claim as she is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.

propositions.text: The panel rejects the refugee claims of the female claimant's four children as derived and based on the same grounds, so outcome is the same.
propositions.quote: The panel also rejects the refugee protection claim filed by the four children of the female claimant, XXXXXXXXX, on the ground that these claims are derived from the female claimant's and have the same basis. Therefore, the outcome for them must be the same.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects the refugee claims of the claimant's four children as derived and based on same grounds.

propositions.text: The co-claimant is a Rwandan citizen claiming refugee protection under sections 96 and 97 of IRPA.
propositions.quote: The co-claimant, XXXXXXXX, is a Rwandan citizen. She is claiming refugee protection in Canada as a refugee, under section 96 of the IRPA, and as a person in need of protection under subsection 97(1) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The co-claimant is a Rwandan citizen claiming refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97.

propositions.text: The co-claimant's claim was heard jointly with her half-sister's and her four minor children’s claims.
propositions.quote: Her claim was heard jointly with the claim filed by her half-sister, XXXXXXXX, and her four minor children, XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX and XXXXXXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The co-claimant's claim was heard jointly with her half-sister's and her four minor children’s claims.

propositions.text: The co-claimant alleged facts supporting her refugee claim.
propositions.quote: The co-claimant alleged the following:

paragraphs.summary: The co-claimant alleged facts supporting her refugee claim.

propositions.text: Since 2006, co-claimant worked part-time in half-sister's business and studied at university.
propositions.quote: Since 2006, she had worked part-time in her half-sister's XXXXXX and had studied at XXXXXXXXXXX University.

propositions.text: In 2009, soldiers demanded bribe from half-sister; police intervened and soldiers were fired and imprisoned.
propositions.quote: She stated that in XXXX 2009, soldiers who worked as inspectors for the "XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX" demanded a bribe from her half-sister to XXXXXXXXXX XXXXXXXXX. The police intervened, and with the cooperation of the two claimants, these people were fired and sentenced to XXXXXX in prison.

propositions.text: After release, female claimant and half-sister received threatening calls.
propositions.quote: After they were released, the female claimant and her half-sister started receiving threatening telephone calls.

paragraphs.summary: Co-claimant worked part-time, soldiers demanded bribe, police intervened, soldiers imprisoned, then threats received.

propositions.text: Co-claimant's claim based on same facts as half-sister; threatened by half-sister's husband after separation; left country after half-sister.
propositions.quote: For the rest, the co-claimant stated that her claim is based on the same facts as those raised by her half-sister, XXXXXXXXX, and that her fears are the same. She added that she was threatened by her half-sister's husband after the couple separated because he blamed her for being complicit with her half-sister. She left the country after her half-sister, by means of a visa that she had obtained in XXXX 2009 for a trip to the United States.

paragraphs.summary: Co-claimant's claim based on same facts as half-sister; threatened by half-sister's husband; left country after half-sister.

propositions.text: The co-claimant's identity was established satisfactorily through testimony and evidence.
propositions.quote: The co-claimant's identity was established to my satisfaction through her testimony and the evidence submitted.

paragraphs.summary: The co-claimant's identity was satisfactorily established through testimony and evidence.

propositions.text: Facts supporting co-claimant's claim are substantially the same as half-sister's; previous analysis applies.
propositions.quote: The facts raised to support her claim are substantially the same as the facts that were raised by her half-sister. Thus, the observations and conclusions in the previous analysis, relating to the claim filed by XXXXXXXXX, also apply to the claim filed by XXXXXXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: Co-claimant's facts are substantially same as half-sister's; previous analysis applies.

propositions.text: The panel determines the co-claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection and rejects her claim.
propositions.quote: Given all these facts and for all these reasons, the panel determines that the co-claimant, XXXXXXXXX, is not a "Convention" refugee or a "person in need of protection," and her refugee protection claim is rejected.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects the co-claimant's refugee protection claim as she is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
